The test image shows a young corn seedling with:
- Pale/white parallel striping on upper leaves
- Lower leaves dead/brown and dried out
- Small seedling in soil

Top candidates: **Downy_mildew** (white parallel stripes, lower leaves dying), **Maize_streak_virus**, **Stewarts_wilt**. Let me check reference images.
The Downy_mildew reference matches very well — young seedlings in soil with white/pale parallel striping. Let me also check Stewarts_wilt and Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus to be thorough.
Stewarts_wilt and MDMV don't match — no parallel striping and different growth stage. Let me check 2 more candidates.

Neither Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma (reddish/purple on older plants) nor Maize_chlorotic_dwarf_virus (vein banding, larger plants) match.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Young corn seedling with prominent **white/pale parallel stripes** running along leaf veins, with lower leaves **dead and brown**
- **Downy_mildew** reference: Exact match — same growth stage (small seedlings in soil), same white parallel striping alternating with green tissue, same lower leaf dieback pattern
- All other candidates ruled out: Maize_streak_virus (older plants, more yellow), Stewarts_wilt (wavy streaks from feeding scars), MDMV (mosaic, not stripes), Corn_Stunt (reddish/purple, larger plants), MCDV (vein banding, larger plants)
